manifest.name: Lensmap
manifest.description: A local-first PDF reading companion that expands context from passages and visuals you choose, then keeps grounded understanding as reusable Maps.

help.heroTitle: Turn what catches your attention into a map of understanding.
help.heroBody: Keep using Chrome’s built-in PDF Viewer, collect passages and visuals into a Reader Workspace, and Explore them. Lensmap can read additional context across multiple PDFs in the Workspace only when needed.
help.languageDescription: Choose the language used by Lensmap. System follows your browser language.
help.step1Body: Open a PDF on the web, or a local PDF after allowing Lensmap to access file URLs.
help.step2Body: “Explore with Lensmap” adds the passage and focuses the question field. “Add to Lensmap references” adds evidence to the current Workspace without starting a question.
help.step3Title: Use “Select region” for figures and tables
help.step3Body: From the Side Panel or context menu, open a frozen Capture Surface of the visible PDF. The cropped image itself is saved as the Visual Source.
help.step4Body: Ask across Text and Visual Sources collected from multiple PDFs in the same Workspace. When needed, Lensmap searches the Workspace and reads relevant sections or nearby context.
help.workspaceBody: A Workspace owns Explore threads, references, and Maps. Switching Chrome tabs does not discard the conversation or draft. References from PDF A and PDF B can live in the same Workspace for comparison.
help.citationsBody: S1 / S2… are the Evidence actually used in the answer. Text Sources show the original passage; Visual Sources show the saved crop thumbnail. When the page has been resolved, a citation returns to that PDF page.
help.citationsNote: Lensmap does not depend on Chrome’s private PDF Viewer API, so it does not promise a permanent rectangle overlay on the source PDF.
help.visualSourceBody: The image crop is the primary information. Apple Vision OCR and PDF-index page resolution are derived metadata for search and preview; if they fail, the image Source remains. When a Visual Source is used in a question, the crop is sent to an image-capable Codex model.
help.aiReferenceBody: A search hit is only a candidate. It becomes S# Evidence only after Codex actually reads that passage. The additional-reading history is also retained as a human-readable summary, including Book names when retrieval crosses PDFs.
help.mapsBody: Each completed Explore answer is automatically saved as one Map, idempotently. Maps containing Visual Sources prioritize the image and retain explanation, Evidence, and version history for later review.
help.codexBody: Lensmap uses Codex App Server as its AI runtime. The control in the upper-right shows the selected model, context usage for the latest turn, and Codex usage windows. Visual Sources require an image-input-capable model; Lensmap does not silently downgrade them to OCR-only input.
help.contextGaugeDefinition: Shows the latest turn’s token usage as a percentage of the model context window reported for that turn.
help.usageWindowDefinition: Rolling rate-limit usage returned by Codex App Server. When multiple windows are reported, Lensmap displays each one.
help.footer: Lensmap keeps PDF content and Visual Sources locally, and sends Codex only the Evidence needed for the current Reader Workspace plus constrained workspace_* retrieval.
